comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official SBE Outline Study Programme for Bachelor Business Engineering 2026-2027 (s2), a nominal plan based on the Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations (Chapter XVI), whose text states the credit structure: the first-year phase has eight compulsory 5-EC courses, two 5-EC skills trainings and two 5-EC projects (60 EC); semesters three and four have four compulsory courses, four electives, two skills trainings and two projects, each 5 EC (60 EC); and semesters five and six comprise one compulsory course, five electives, one skills training and one project of 5 EC each, plus the 2.5-EC Introduction to the thesis and the 17.5-EC Thesis Research Project, which the outline records together as the 20-EC BENP2004 (60 EC). Every course's 5-EC weight (20 EC for the thesis project) and content was verified in the UM Course Descriptions Application (s4, 2026-2027 calendar). The public courses-and-curriculum page (s1) is labelled 2024-2025 and lists the same compulsory courses, skills trainings and projects without EC weights; the 2025-2026 outline (s3) differs from 2026-2027 only in the timetabling of periods, not in course titles or codes. The programme has no formal routes, tracks or specializations. The nine 'Year 2+3 Elective' slots are genuine open elective space: the official outline prescribes no content for them, so they are preserved as electives of 5 EC each rather than filled with invented courses. The Education and Examination Regulations were not consulted separately because the outline reproduces their credit text and no conflict between official sources was found.

core: Business-engineering integration: connecting engineering, science and business to analyse and solve complex technological business problems, including the engineering design cycle and the link between engineering problems and business processes
Mathematics for engineering and business: single-variable and multivariable calculus and linear algebra, with numerical and computational aspects
Statistics, data analysis and experimentation: data collection, inference, regression and the statistical testing of technical and business ideas
Software and computing skills: software tools, SQL, programming in an imperative and object-oriented language, and algorithms and complexity
Physical-science and engineering principles: mechanics, energy, materials and production processes

Product and process design and sustainability engineering: designing products and production processes under technical and business constraints, with circular-economy and life-cycle assessment projects
Economics, finance and business functions: micro- and macroeconomics, markets, and corporate finance and investment decisions
Commercialising science and technology: market opportunity identification, market research and value creation from technological inventions
Ethics and people skills in engineering and business practice: responsible decision-making, and organisational leadership and communication
Research and development and independent research: laboratory and research skills, an R&D project with an external research question and a bachelor thesis
adjacent: Computational and software-oriented engineering: programming, computational methods and software development applied to engineering analysis and product development
questions: Turning technological inventions into viable, sustainable and responsible businesses by combining engineering, science and business

trace: teaches problem solving and programming in Python, from structured programming and data constructs through testing, debugging and object-oriented constructs, and directly implements the programming-language and imperative and object-oriented paradigm content of the target's Computer Science Skills; it is also the formal prerequisite for the software, algorithm and optimisation courses

teaches the physics, chemistry, materials-science, mathematics and modelling concepts needed to analyse sustainability problems and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's Fundamentals of Engineering (basic engineering principles, elementary modelling and energy); it is not a substitute for the target's mechanics, electricity, fluids and heat-transfer content, and it is the formal prerequisite for Sustainability Essentials II

covers supply and demand, consumer theory, the theory of the firm and market structures in microeconomics and aggregate output, unemployment, inflation and goods and financial markets in macroeconomics, and directly implements the micro- and macroeconomic content of the target's Economics for Business Engineering

teaches differentiation, techniques of integration, complex numbers and differential equations through applied projects and directly implements the single-variable calculus, integration and differential-equation content of the target's Calculus; it is also the formal prerequisite for the linear algebra, probability and statistics, advanced calculus, numerical and systems courses

teaches research design, operationalisation, experimental design, sampling, surveys and descriptive and inferential statistics including analysis of variance, and directly implements the data-collection, estimation and hypothesis-testing content of the target's Statistics; it also makes a specific complementary contribution to the experimental design of Experimentation in Science and Engineering, and is the formal prerequisite for the market-research and econometrics-type courses

builds on Sustainability Essentials I with a focus on waves, chemistry and materials science and their relation to sustainability, and directly addresses the materials-science part of the target's Materials Engineering; it does not teach the engineering-materials classification, production and characterisation methods of that component, and it is the formal prerequisite for Renewable System Design and R3

teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation of tabular, spatial and text data in a programming environment and ends in the student's own data-analysis project, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's Statistics (using software to summarise data numerically and visually) and its software skills training; it does not teach SQL databases

has teams develop a venture idea from ideation through market validation and business planning to a final pitch and directly addresses the opportunity-identification and evaluation part of the target's Commercialising Science and Technology; it is not specific to science-based inventions, and it is the formal prerequisite for the strategy, finance and market-research courses

teaches probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation and makes a specific complementary contribution to the estimation and inference foundations of the target's Statistics

has students evaluate the environmental impact of products and processes over their whole life cycle with life-cycle-assessment methods and circular-economy strategies, and directly implements the target's Circular Economy Project (Life Cycle Assessment)
teaches systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, linear independence and linear transformations and directly implements the target's Linear Algebra

teaches software development in C++ and Haskell, including requirements gathering, testing, quality assurance and code review, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the programming-paradigm content of the target's Computer Science Skills and to its software skills

teaches the assessment of energy-use patterns and the design of solar, wind and bioenergy solutions through technical and economic analysis, ending in a report and presentation for a partner company, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the energy-engineering and real-company case work of the target's Process and Product Design Project; UCR has no manufacturing or production engineering course

is a team project course on a sustainability research problem posed by an external regional company or institution, with a project plan, data analysis and a research report, and directly addresses the externally posed research question, project plan and data analysis of the target's Research and Development Project

has teams take a consumer product through customer-needs analysis, product concept, quantitative modelling of its working mechanism, laboratory experiments, prototype, industrial-scale production method, sustainability, cost and proceeds analysis, and directly implements the concept-to-production design cycle of the target's Process and Product Design Project

examines circular-economy strategies and technologies for recycling, recovery and remediation and develops laboratory skills and inorganic chemistry knowledge, and directly addresses the laboratory-skills part of the target's Laboratory and Research Skills; it does not reproduce that component's industrial-process experiments

teaches organisational behaviour including motivation, leadership, communication, group dynamics, power, conflict and negotiation, organisational culture and change through cases and skill-building, and directly addresses the leadership and interpersonal-skills content of the target's Organisational Leadership and People Skills

teaches sustainable engineering design with natural processes, such as ecosystem-based design for flood protection, land reclamation and port development, through case studies and field excursions, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the engineering-design content of the target's Fundamentals of Engineering and its sustainability-oriented engineering projects; it is not a substitute for the target's mechanical and process engineering

has students plan and carry out real market research, analyse the data and present the results, and directly implements the research-design, data-collection, analysis and reporting content of the target's Market Research Project
extends calculus to several variables and to differential equations with computer algebra software and directly implements the multivariable calculus content of the target's Multivariable Calculus

has students develop a strategic plan from vision to execution and identify digital value opportunities using industry cases, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the management-planning and business-strategy content of the target's Introduction to Business Engineering and its economics-and-strategy integration; it is not a substitute for the target's engineering-management content

develops financial-decision skills through case studies, including analysing financial data, assessing risk and making investment and budgeting decisions, and directly addresses the investment-decision and risk part of the target's Corporate Finance and Investment; it does not teach capital-market functioning or asset pricing as such

teaches the main ethical theories (virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism) and applies them to practical ethical questions such as responsibility, climate change and future generations, and directly addresses the ethical frameworks of the target's Ethical and Philosophical Reflections; it does not treat engineering-specific cases

teaches numerical differentiation, root finding and the numerical solution of differential equations and optimisation problems with computer algebra software, and directly addresses the computational and numerical aspects that the target's Calculus and Multivariable Calculus highlight through Mathematica and MATLAB

teaches how linear time-invariant systems are characterised and respond to signals through transfer functions, state-space models and differential equations, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the elementary modelling of energy and electrical systems in the target's Fundamentals of Engineering; it is a mathematical systems course rather than a practical engineering course

teaches algorithm design and analysis with experimental performance analysis of algorithms and data structures, and directly implements the algorithms-and-complexity content of the target's Computer Science Skills

teaches search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation by rational agents and makes a specific complementary contribution to the optimisation of production choices in the target's Process and Product Engineering and to computational problem-solving of complex technological problems; it does not teach production processes

teaches linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage and tree-based methods on real-world data and makes a specific complementary contribution to the regression modelling and data-based decision content of the target's Statistics

teaches robotics and industrial automation, with forward and inverse kinematics, motion planning and robotic grasping, and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's engineering-principles and production-automation content; it is a computational robotics course, not a manufacturing-process course

addresses fairness, bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability in AI and makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's Ethical and Philosophical Reflections, which examines responsible decision-making and the impact of technology on society, for the computational technologies emphasised in this alternative

teaches planning techniques for AI systems under uncertainty, including resource planning and optimising behaviour under constraints, and makes a specific complementary contribution to solving complex technological problems and to the production and project planning content of the target's Introduction to Business Engineering

alternatives.label: Closest match to Business Engineering: Sustainability Engineering, Quantitative Methods and Business
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has four substantial strands: seven courses in UCR's environment and sustainability engineering cluster (Sustainability Essentials I and II, Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, Building with Nature, Renewable System Design, R3 and Research in a Sustainable Delta), seven in business, economics and finance (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics, Money Banking & Finance, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, Consumer Product Design and Psychology of Organizations & Leadership), five in mathematics and statistics (Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Advanced Calculus, Probability & Statistics and Research Methods & Statistics), and three in programming, software and data (Introduction to Programming, Software Development and Introduction to Data Science), plus Ethics and Personal & Professional Development. A single-field label would hide at least one of these strands, so the label names the engineering, quantitative and business strands that mirror the target's own integration of engineering, science and business, and 'closest match to Business Engineering' makes clear that UCR offers no engineering degree curriculum.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the Bachelor Business Engineering at Maastricht University: a programme that reproduces the target's own integration of engineering, science and business. It pairs the mathematics (calculus, linear algebra, statistics) and computing foundations of the target's first two years with UCR's sustainability-engineering courses (physical-science essentials, life-cycle assessment and circular economy, energy-system design, laboratory skills and an externally posed research project) and with UCR's product-design, entrepreneurship, market-research, economics, finance, strategy, organisational-leadership and ethics courses that correspond to the target's commercialisation, project, finance and reflection components. UCR offers no materials, manufacturing or mechanical engineering courses, no engineering-management course and no thesis, and those limitations are preserved in the comparison.
progression: DISGATE101 (semester 1), DISGATE102, BENGATE102 and ENSGATE201 (semester 2, following ENSGATE101 and BENGATE101 in semester 1) and BENGATE101 (semester 1), none of which lacks its own prerequisites in an earlier semester, precede every course that formally requires them: BENBUSI312 (semester 2, requires BENGATE101 from semester 1); DISMATH211 and DISMATH314 (semester 3, require DISGATE102); DISCOMP213 (semester 4, requires DISGATE101); ENSSUST311 (semester 4, requires ENSGATE201); ENSDELT311 (semester 5, requires ENSGATE201); BENLEAD311 (semester 5, requires BENGATE102); and BENENTR311, BENENTR212 (semester 6, require BENGATE101) and DISMATH214 (semester 6, requires DISGATE102). Personal & Professional Development is in semester 1. Advisory progression is followed where feasible: mathematics, programming, sustainability-science gateway and business-foundation courses are concentrated in semesters 1-3, followed by applied engineering, design, project and leadership courses in semesters 4-5, and advanced calculus, strategy and market research in semester 6. Two courses are placed later than the target's first-year logic would suggest (Introduction to Economics in semester 3, Building with Nature in semester 5) because no formal prerequisite requires an earlier placement, and Research in a Sustainable Delta is scheduled in semester 4 because it has no formal prerequisite and is offered then.

alternatives.label: Computational Modelling, Data and Technology Business
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has 15 courses in mathematics, computer science, AI and data (Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Advanced Calculus, Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems, Probability & Statistics, Introduction to Programming, Software Development, Algorithms & Data Structures, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI, Robotics and AI Ethics) and 7 in business and economics (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics, Money Banking & Finance, Strategy & Digital Transformation, Market Research, Consumer Product Design and Research Methods & Statistics), plus one team research project and Personal & Professional Development. The label names the computational and data-modelling majority first and the technology-business strand second; it does not use 'engineering' because UCR offers no engineering degree curriculum.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second route built on the computational core of the target rather than its sustainability-engineering and physical-science strand: the target's Software Skills, Computer Science Skills, calculus and linear-algebra sequence and its emphasis on software and computational problem-solving in engineering analysis and product development are extended into a programme organised around computational modelling. It combines UCR's full mathematics track with programming, software development, algorithms, optimisation, planning, machine learning, systems modelling and robotics, and keeps the target's business half through entrepreneurship, economics, finance, strategy, market research and consumer product design, with an AI-ethics course for responsible technology and one externally posed research project.
alternatives.distinctness: Alternative 1 reproduces the target's engineering-science and sustainability-engineering strand (Sustainability Essentials I and II, Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, Building with Nature, Renewable System Design and R3) together with organisational leadership and general ethics; this alternative removes that strand, plus Psychology of Organizations & Leadership and Ethics, and replaces the eight courses with the computational core that is organised by the target's programming and computer-science skills and by the software and computational problem-solving programme interest: Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems, Algorithms & Data Structures, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI, Machine Learning, Robotics and AI Ethics. The two programmes therefore share 16 courses (the common mathematics, business and project courses) and each has 8 courses (60 EC) that the other lacks, which is above the 30-EC floor; the differing courses are the consequences of choosing a computational-modelling organising logic instead of a sustainability-engineering one, not arbitrary substitutions, and they change the programme's central academic priority from physical and environmental engineering systems to mathematical, algorithmic and data-driven problem-solving.
progression: DISGATE101 (semester 1) precedes DISCOMP213 (semester 4), DISCOMP311 (semester 3), DISARIN211 (semester 5) and DISARIN311 (semester 6), all of which formally require it; DISGATE102 (semester 2) precedes DISMATH211, DISMATH314 (semester 3), DISMATH213, DISMATH312, DISDATA312 (semester 4) and DISMATH214 (semester 6), all of which formally require it; BENGATE101 (semester 1) precedes BENBUSI312 (semester 2), BENENTR212 and BENENTR311 (semester 6), and BENGATE102 (semester 2) is a prerequisite of none of the selected courses. Personal & Professional Development is in semester 1. Advisory progression is followed where feasible: mathematics, programming and business foundations are in semesters 1-2, probability, statistics, algorithms and data science in semester 3 (following Mathematical Methods and Introduction to Programming), numerical methods, linear systems, robotics and software development in semester 4 (following Linear Algebra), and machine learning, planning and the applied project in semester 5, followed by optimisation and advanced calculus in semester 6. Machine Learning (semester 5) follows Probability & Statistics and Linear Algebra.

selection.assessment: Alternative 1 directly owns eleven generator-eligible rows that describe the programme's own integration of engineering, science and business (5656, 5657, 5658, 5659, 5661, 5662, 5669, 5670, 5671, 5675, 5676): the integrated identity and complex technological business problems, commercialising technology and scientific research, mathematics, economics and business strategy, statistics and experimentation, research and development, product and process design, ethics and responsible innovation, and independent business-engineering research. Three candidate directions were then assessed against the four gates. (1) Computational and software-oriented engineering (generating row 5664, 'software and computational problem-solving', supported by 5658, 5659, 5660 and 5662) is evidenced by the target's Software Skills and Computer Science Skills trainings and its mathematics and statistics sequence, is coherent as a computational-modelling organising logic, is feasible, and yields a curriculum that shares 16 courses with Alternative 1 and has 8 courses (60 EC) that Alternative 1 lacks; it is included as Alternative 2. (2) Laboratory experimentation and applied science research (generating row 5673, supported by the curricular-topic rows 5660 and 5663) is rejected for insufficient evidence: the target's laboratory work is materials, physics and process-engineering experimentation, whereas UCR's only laboratory course is the Life Science Laboratory, whose biology content has no evidence in the target; the laboratory content that the evidence does support (R3 and Research in a Sustainable Delta) is already in Alternative 1, so the direction cannot form a distinct 24-course programme. (3) Project management and interdisciplinary team leadership (generating rows 5665 and 5674) is rejected for insufficient evidence: both rows describe skills-training elements that the target delivers as skills courses and projects, they do not evidence a separate programme, and a programme organised around UCR's leadership and communication courses would drop the engineering and science content that defines the target. Ethics and responsible innovation (row 5675) is substantively covered by Alternative 1's Ethics course and the target's own Ethical and Philosophical Reflections, and does not imply a genuinely different route. No further adjacent direction or question with target-specific evidence remains, and the outcome-only and illustrative interest rows are search-only and cannot generate an alternative, so production stops at two alternatives.

Mathematical Methods directly addresses the differentiation, integration and differential-equation content of Calculus; the target's limits, sequences and series and approximation theory are not specifically covered.

Linear Algebra directly addresses Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations; the target's eigenvalue and orthogonality content is treated within the same subject.

Research Methods & Statistics directly addresses the data-collection, sampling, descriptive and inferential statistics and hypothesis-testing content of Statistics; the target's multiple-regression modelling is covered only at an introductory level.
Advanced Calculus directly addresses Multivariable Calculus: calculus in several variables and differential equations with computer algebra software.
Engineering principles, materials, laboratory work and engineering systems

Sustainability Essentials I directly addresses an important and identifiable part of Fundamentals of Engineering's subject, the physics, mathematics and modelling of energy and materials used to analyse real systems; it does not teach the mechanics, electricity, fluids, heat-transfer or design-cycle content of that component, and the difference in scope is material.

Sustainability Essentials II directly addresses the materials-science part of Materials Engineering (with chemistry and waves); it does not teach engineering-materials classification, production and characterisation methods.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Experimentation in Science and Engineering trains students to plan and perform basic laboratory experiments; no scheduled UCR course in either alternative provides that hands-on experimental introduction, and research-design content is on another row.

R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation directly addresses the laboratory-skills part of Laboratory and Research Skills together with inorganic chemistry; it does not reproduce the target's industrial-process experiments or its research-question-to-experiment training.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Process and Product Engineering covers production, manufacturing and assembly processes and production calculations; no scheduled UCR course addresses manufacturing or production engineering as an important part of its content.

Introduction to Programming directly addresses the programming-language and imperative and object-oriented paradigm content of Computer Science Skills; the target's algorithms-and-complexity foundations are treated on a separate row.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Software Skills teaches a range of software tools including SQL queries in Microsoft Access; no scheduled UCR course addresses that tool-based skills content as an important and identifiable part of its subject, since the data-science course rests on programming rather than these tools.
Product and process design, sustainability engineering and applied projects

Consumer Product Design directly addresses the product-concept, design-and-development team and production-method content of Process and Product Design Project, including sustainability and cost analysis; it does not analyse an existing industrial product's manufacturing cycle.
Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy directly implements Circular Economy Project (Life Cycle Assessment): life-cycle assessment and circular-economy strategies applied to products and processes.

Research in a Sustainable Delta directly addresses the research-project format of Research and Development Project: an externally posed research problem, a project plan, data analysis and a report; its topics are sustainability rather than engineering.
Introduction to Economics directly implements Economics for Business Engineering: microeconomics, market structures and macroeconomics.
Market Research directly implements Market Research Project: planning and carrying out market research, analysing the data and reporting the results.

Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations directly addresses the opportunity-identification, market-validation and business-planning part of Commercialising Science and Technology; it is generic venture creation rather than the commercialisation of science-based inventions.

Money, Banking & Finance directly addresses the investment, risk and budgeting-decision part of Corporate Finance and Investment; it does not teach capital-market functioning or asset pricing as such.
Ethics directly addresses the ethical frameworks and their application to responsible decision-making in Ethical and Philosophical Reflections; it does not use engineering-specific cases.
Psychology of Organizations & Leadership directly addresses the leadership, communication and interpersonal-skills content of Organisational Leadership and People Skills.

notes.text: The Bachelor Business Engineering combines Fundamentals of Engineering, Materials Engineering, Process and Product Engineering and experimental laboratory training with business and management. At UCR, students can approach engineering, science and technology through fields such as sustainability and environmental engineering, mathematics, computer science and data science alongside business, economics and finance. These programmes therefore offer related perspectives rather than reproducing a full engineering or materials-science curriculum: UCR has no mechanical, materials or manufacturing engineering courses.

The Bachelor Business Engineering reserves nine 5-EC electives (45 EC, whose content the official outline does not fix) and a 20-EC thesis project, about 65 EC of the target's curriculum, as open or independent-research space that no UCR course can defensibly represent. The UCR programmes instead distribute comparable territory across their own courses in sustainability, mathematics, computing, economics and business, so they cover related ground through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the target course by course.
